newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Industry Minister may leave party - paper.
newsitem.headline: Czech Industry Minister may leave party - paper.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy will resign from the right-wing Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) if he is not happy with the result of the election of a new party chief, the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes reported on Monday.
"If someone is elected (as head) that to me does not guarantee our party will remain in parliament and realise the party's programme, I'm ready to leave," Dlouhy said in an interview with the paper.
The ODA gained just under seven percent of the vote in spring general elections, just over the five percent minimum needed to gain entrance to parliament.
Dlouhy consistently polls as the country's most popular politician, scoring well above Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and even higher than President Vaclav Havel.

In mid-December, the ODA was forced to call a leadership convention for March when party leader Jan Kalvoda resigned after he admitted using a phoney academic title. Kalvoda also resigned as a deputy premier, Justice Minister and left his parliamentary seat.
The ODA has four posts in the 16-member cabinet.
Two factions within the ODA, one linked with Dlouhy and the other with minister at large Pavel Bratinka, are expected to fight for control of the party.
In the interview Dlouhy said he does not know if he will be a candidate in the race, and he would not name any possible candidates that he would support.

The governing coalition, which consists of Klaus's centre-right ODS, and junior coalition partners ODA and KDU-CSL, lost its majority in the spring elections, garnering 99 seats in the 200-seat lower house of parliament.
